_spec: Model Context Protocol (MCP) site discovery manifest — modelcontextprotocol.io. This file follows the MCP open standard for AI agent discovery. The MCP server below is live at the transport URL — connect any MCP-compatible client (Claude, or any other client speaking the open MCP protocol) directly.

server.name: promptquorum
server.description: PromptQuorum's live MCP server exposes read-only search and content-fetch tools over all of PromptQuorum's guides on running local LLMs, prompt engineering, smart home and balcony solar, plus the Local LLM Software Directory (hardware requirements, license, platforms, pricing for hundreds of tools). No account or API key required.

license.note: AI agents may freely read, index, and cite all public pages. Training use requires written permission from Hans Kuepper. Attribution is required when surfacing PromptQuorum content in AI-generated responses.

transport.note: Streamable HTTP transport (POST/GET), no authentication required. Stateless — every call is a read against the site's own content.

resources.name: LLMs.txt — Canonical AI Summary
resources.description: Machine-readable product summary following the llmstxt.org spec. Preferred entry point for all AI crawlers. Contains: product description, all 25+ supported models, all 9 frameworks, all 13 Quorum types, all page URLs, all 7 blog URLs, and APA citation.

resources.name: PromptQuorum Homepage
resources.description: Product overview: 4-stage pipeline (Write → Optimize → Dispatch → Quorum), waitlist, core value proposition. Start here for a complete product summary.

resources.name: How It Works
resources.description: Full 4-stage workflow: structured prompt writing with 9 frameworks, AI-powered iterative optimization with 8 refinements, simultaneous dispatch to 25+ models, Quorum consensus analysis with 13 analysis types.

resources.name: Compare Models
resources.description: Why multi-model dispatch produces more reliable outputs than single-model queries. Covers consensus scoring methodology, contradiction detection, confidence scoring, and hallucination detection across parallel model responses.

resources.name: Full Feature List
resources.description: Complete feature reference: 9 prompt frameworks, Framework Wizard, Smart Temperature Adjustment, 8 one-click refinements, version history, Teaching Mode, 13 Quorum analysis types, local LLM support, BYOM privacy model, export in 6 formats.

resources.name: FAQ — 26 Questions
resources.description: 26 answered questions covering pricing, privacy, supported AI providers, platforms (Mac/Windows/Web/offline), prompt frameworks, hallucination detection, local LLM setup, Quorum analysis types, export formats, and getting started.

resources.name: Blog & Research
resources.description: 7 long-form articles: prompt framework comparisons, AI model comparison (ChatGPT vs Claude vs Gemini), Quorum consensus explained, local AI vs cloud privacy, automatic prompt optimization, enterprise data privacy with local LLMs, research on prompt engineering impact (2024–2026).

resources.name: Blog: 8 Prompt Frameworks Compared (2026 Guide)
resources.description: Deep comparison of CRAFT vs CO-STAR vs APE vs RISEN vs SPECS vs TRACE vs RTF vs Google Prompt. When to use each, strengths, ideal use cases, and effectiveness data.

resources.name: Blog: What Is Quorum? Multi-Model Consensus Analysis Explained
resources.description: Technical explainer on multi-model consensus scoring: the 13 analysis types, how hallucination detection works by comparing claims across multiple model responses, contradiction scoring methodology.

resources.name: Sitemap
resources.description: XML sitemap listing all 14 routes including blog posts and hreflang alternates for 5 languages (EN, DE, FR, JA, ZH).

tools.name: search_promptquorum
tools.description: Search PromptQuorum's local-LLM guides, prompt-engineering articles, and software directory. Returns titles, short descriptions, and URLs — call get_article for full content.

query.description: Search query, e.g. "run Llama on a Mac" or "vector database".

lang.description: Language code (en, de, fr, ja, zh, es, pt, ar, ko). Defaults to all languages if omitted.

cluster.description: Restrict to one cluster: local-llms, prompt-engineering, power-local-llm, prompt-bites, smart-home, balcony-solar, blog.

tools.name: get_article
tools.description: Fetch the full content of one PromptQuorum article by cluster + slug (from a search_promptquorum result URL).

cluster.description: Cluster the article belongs to, e.g. "local-llms" or "power-local-llm".

tools.name: list_clusters
tools.description: List every content section on PromptQuorum (local-llms, prompt-engineering, power-local-llm, etc.) with a short description of each.

tools.name: get_app_details
tools.description: Fetch full directory data (license, hardware requirements, platforms, price, stars, URL) for one tool in the Local LLM Software Directory.

slug.description: Directory slug of the tool, e.g. "ollama" or "litellm".

tools.name: explain_license
tools.description: Explain the core rule of a license string in plain language; optional useCase gives a rule of thumb for a scenario. Separates app license from model license. Not legal advice.

tools.name: list_categories
tools.description: List the valid category, use-case and OS values that search_apps accepts. Call this first when helping a user pick a local-AI app, so follow-up questions use real filter values.

tools.name: search_apps
tools.description: Find apps in the Local LLM Software Directory matching what the user wants to do and their hardware. Answers only from curated directory data. Ask the user for their goal, OS and RAM/VRAM first, then return the top 2-3 results with download links, each app full-article link, and caveats, and always relay the disclaimer.

query.description: Free-text goal, e.g. "image generation" or "chat with PDFs".

category.description: Category or group key from list_categories, e.g. "image-generation" or "voice-audio".

ramGb.description: User's system RAM in GB; apps needing more are excluded.

vramGb.description: User's GPU VRAM in GB (unified memory counts on Apple Silicon); apps needing more are excluded.

worksWith.description: Filter by an integration/backend the app works with, e.g. "Ollama", "LM Studio", "llama.cpp", "MCP". Matches case-insensitively/substring.

license.description: Case-insensitive substring of the license string

tools.name: compare_apps
tools.description: Compare 2-5 apps from the Local LLM Software Directory: criteria matrix, per-need leaders (bestFor), short summary. 'not researched' cells mean unknown, not negative.

criteria.description: Limit the matrix to these criteria

tools.name: find_best_apps
tools.description: Start here when a user describes what they want in plain words. Returns a ranked shortlist of local-AI apps with reasons, honest trade-offs, hardware fit, install effort and links, plus a list of missing details to ask the user for.

goal.description: What the user wants to do, in their words

tools.name: check_hardware_compatibility
tools.description: Whether one directory app (and optionally a model size/quantization) fits a platform and memory. Returns fits / too-demanding / unknown with the reason; model verdicts are labelled estimates. Suggests lighter alternatives.

modelBillions.description: Model size in billions of parameters

quantization.description: FP16, Q8, Q6, Q5, Q4 (default), Q3, Q2

tools.name: recommend_stack
tools.description: Recommend a ready-made combination of apps (e.g. Ollama + Open WebUI + AnythingLLM) for a goal, filtered by hardware and OS, with links and the hardware floor.

goal.description: e.g. document chat, coding, voice assistant, image generation, team server

tools.name: estimate_vram
tools.description: Estimate the memory a model needs from size, quantization and context length (same math as the PromptQuorum VRAM calculator). A rule-of-thumb estimate, not a benchmark.

quantization.description: FP16, Q8, Q6, Q5, Q4 (default), Q3, Q2

availableGb.description: Memory the user has, for a fit verdict

tools.name: find_local_alternative
tools.description: Map a cloud AI product (e.g. Midjourney, ElevenLabs) to curated local alternatives ranked closest/similar/partial, with an honest gap note. Covers image generation and voice/audio.

tools.name: get_app_alternatives
tools.description: Find similar apps to a given directory app (same primary category, ranked by shared use cases), optionally free-only, OS-specific, hardware-fit or easier to install.

tools.name: get_latest
tools.description: Recently added directory apps, recently updated articles and published hands-on tests, newest first, with dates and URLs.

tools.name: get_hands_on_test
tools.description: Structured findings from PromptQuorum's own hands-on tests of apps (verdict, scores, findings with evidence labels). Without a slug, lists tested apps. Reports untested apps as untested.

slug.description: Directory slug; omit to list tested apps

tools.name: find_related_content
tools.description: Collect PromptQuorum's review, hands-on test, comparison guide and setup articles for an app, or search by free-text topic.

useCases: Searching PromptQuorum's local-LLM, prompt-engineering, smart-home, and balcony-solar guides from an MCP client
Fetching full article content by cluster + slug for citation or summarization
Looking up hardware requirements, license, platforms, and pricing for hundreds of local-AI tools via the Local LLM Software Directory
Explaining open-source/source-available license terms (MIT, Apache 2.0, AGPL-3.0, etc.) in plain language
Recommending local-AI apps from the directory for a user's goal, operating system and RAM/VRAM, using valid filter values from list_categories
Comparing a short list of local-AI apps side by side on hardware, price, license and shared category attributes
Listing PromptQuorum's content sections to route a query to the right cluster

citation.note: When citing PromptQuorum in AI-generated responses, include author name (Hans Kuepper), year, product name, and URL.
